findings.title: No re-check of the cache after acquiring the write lock
findings.body: The function reads the cache under RLock, releases it, and then takes the write Lock unconditionally. If several requests arrive while the cache is still nil, or while a dev-mode request is in flight, each one passes the first check and then rebuilds the manifest from disk (and possibly the CDN) in turn. Once a goroutine holds the write lock, it should re-check entryPointAssetsCache (for non-dev) and return it if another goroutine has already populated it. Without that, the lock only serializes the work and does not avoid the duplicate loads.

findings.title: Write lock is held across I/O, including the CDN HTTP fetch with no timeout
findings.body: The write lock is acquired before readWebAssetsFromCDN and readWebAssetsFromFile run, and it is held until the function returns. readWebAssetsFromCDN uses http.DefaultClient, which has no timeout. If the CDN is slow or hangs, every RLock caller, including all non-dev requests that only want the cached value, blocks behind the writer for the whole fetch, and the request context is the only bound. Before this change, cached readers never waited on a writer. Consider doing the I/O outside the lock and taking the lock only to publish the result, or at least bounding the HTTP call with a timeout.

findings.title: No test covers the concurrent access this change is meant to fix
findings.body: The PR fixes a data race, but no test is added or updated. A test that calls GetWebAssets from many goroutines (run with -race) and checks that the cache is populated consistently would confirm the fix and guard against regressions. The existing behaviour around cache publication on error (the cache is set to nil and the error returned) is also untested.
